where: tools/full-unchanged.sh + tests/full-unchanged.html + tools/_fu_compare.py (the lock as a whole), commit 4ea395bb
what: A Simple release carrying 16 changes to Full gets a literal PASS, and the ship.sh gate says OK. Each change was confirmed live in a real browser, meaning it really changes Full. The 16, grouped by cause (details in the findings below): (A) his phone width 440 px: the transport skip margin; short screens ≤720 px tall: view-bar gaps. (B) a friend's edit arriving in Full now shows 'A friend moved N clips' (DESIGN V12). (C) every saved project record gains `ed`, and every Home index card gains `ed` and `clips` (DESIGN I15). (D) the reduced-motion path; the dark Home top bar. (E) the toast sits 24 px higher on the phone; the 'Benchmark removed' toast is reworded. (F) the cog's Canvas↔Friends flight goes from 460 ms with its spring curve to 700 ms ease-in-out. (G) the inspector card's hover glow; the menu-item hover colour. (H) a one-finger swipe over a clip scrubs 1.5× as far. (I) the export soundtrack drops from 160 to 96 kb/s. (J) Brightness defaults to 1.2 instead of 1.3. (K) F zooms the timeline. A 17th change, the clip hold going from 350 to 500 ms, also compared 'same as HEAD'. It was stopped only by an accident: it overwrote the touch plant's anchor line.

Patch at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-ezrasmith-Claude-FreeMotion/fde0eeaf-7d73-45b8-9f83-7761553e344d/scratchpad/rv926/simple-release-16.patch; full log in rv926/e2e2.out. Running FU_MAX_LOAD=8 tools/full-unchanged.sh printed: 'both sides measured in 1213s', '✅ same as HEAD (62 pictures compared …)', all 26 plants '✅ … caught', then 'PASS — Full is unchanged against HEAD (4ea395bb) … Cached for sources 0aace2d7e26ff5e544cb989d'. Then `python3 tools/_fu_gate.py check` printed 'OK: full-unchanged PASS on this tree …' (rc 0). where: tools/_fu_gate.py simple_owned_lines() / is_simple_commit() (provenance), via hook_lines() in check()
what: After the first Simple release ships, every ordinary release is refused. ship.sh commits one release as one commit, and that commit includes index.html's version label and every ?v= buster it bumped. git blame then credits those lines to the Simple commit. The next ordinary release has to bump the version label (and any shared buster), so 'the diff changes a line a Simple release wrote' fires. The release is then refused for naming another queue item. Even without that, it would need a PASS it can never get, because it changes Full on purpose. There is no override, so #482 batches, hunt fixes and every other Full change would stop the day Simple ships. The gate's self-test misses this because its scratch Simple release never touches a version label or a buster.
verified_by: Scratch clone of 4ea395bb. Commit 7f30ebcb 'v17.24 — queue 980 (partial)': new js/spine.js, a 'Simple mode' hook line in js/app.js, app.js?v= and storage.js?v= bumped, label v17.24. Then an uncommitted ordinary release: one styles.css rule, styles.css?v=754, label v17.25, log '- v17.25 — queue 975 …'. `python3 tools/_fu_gate.py check` → 'REFUSE: this is a Simple release (the diff changes a line a Simple release wrote in index.html (~@@ -268 +268 @@ changes line 268 of HEAD, which Simple release 7f30ebcb wrote)), and the newest POLISH-LOG line also names queue 975 …' (rc 1). `why` gives the same reason. The self-test still reports ✅.
fix: In simple_owned_lines, skip a hunk when every removed/added pair is identical after masking the version label (>v\d+(\.\d+)*<) and ?v=<number>. A pure insertion between two such lines should not count either. Add a selftest_repo case: a Simple commit that bumps the label and busters, followed by an ordinary release that bumps them again, must be NOT-TRIGGERED.

what: The 'two-release route' is closed only for four settings: FU_INVISIBLE keys, the tolerance numbers, plant names and PNG_UNSTABLE. Any other loosening of the probe or comparer goes unnoticed, so the fixer's claim that the route is closed holds only for those four. Example: an ordinary release that switches off FU6's comparison in _fu_compare.py and drops 'box-shadow' from the probe's STYLES gets NOT-TRIGGERED. Logged as queue 980 instead, it needs only a PASS. That PASS compares HEAD against itself with plants, and no plant covers FU6 or box-shadow (FU6 has no plant at all), so it passes. No LOOSENS THE LOCK line is ever asked for, and the next release (Simple) is then judged by the weaker instrument. The lock's suite guards do not check STYLES or the FU6 comparison either.

where: tests/full-unchanged.html FU4 (startSession: the guest is plainAdapter and never edits) and FU1's session screen (presence only)
what: How Full reacts when a friend edits is never driven. The guest engine sends nothing but presence and acks, and FU4 records only what the host sends. So any change to Full's receiving side passes, including DESIGN's own V12 ('Sam moved 4 clips' toasts in Full, removed). The change tested: in collab-session.js applyIncoming, a `toast('A friend moved N clips')` when a peer's ops land (!oo.own && oo.by !== S.mid). The join path (collab-ui.js admission, 'Sam joined' toast) is never run either.
verified_by: Literal PASS in the 16-change run. Liveness: rv926/work/v12check.html, where the host shares, a loopback guest moves a clip 0.5 s, then G.tick + settle. HEAD: hostStartAfter 0.5, no toasts. Changed: 'A friend moved 1 clip' (rv926/v12-head.json, v12-smug2.json). A first version keyed on collab-bridge afterApply was caught, because it also fired on the host's own ⌘Z (FU4 steps 15/16). This one fires only on a peer's edit, and nothing caught it.

what: Only held touch drags are driven, so the most common phone gestures and the hold thresholds are not measured. scrubrate: timeline.js scrubs the playhead 1.5× as far when a finger swipes over a clip (`FM.scrubTime(snapT(clipTap.baseTime - 1.5 * …))`). hold500: the clip hold went 350 → 500 ms and still compared '✅ same as HEAD' at both widths in the first lock run. Only the touch plant (whose anchor is that exact line) stopped it, with the misleading remedy 'update tools/full-unchanged-plants.json'. where: tests/full-unchanged.html mp4Info / decodedGrid / 'export frames and audio'
what: The exported file's sound is never compared. mp4Info keeps the track sample count, stts and an stsd hash (mp4-muxer writes a constant esds bitrate), the decoded grid is video only, and exportAudio is the mix built before encoding. audiobr: exporter.js encodeAudio `bitrate: 160000` → 96000, so the soundtrack of every MP4 export loses quality.
verified_by: Literal PASS in the 16-change run. Liveness: AudioEncoder.prototype.configure wrapped during FM.exporter.run: bitrates [160000, 160000] on HEAD, [160000, 96000] changed. The first is the priming probe; the second is the real encode (live.json).
fix: Record a hash of the stsz sample-size table (or each track's total sample bytes). Decode the exported file's audio (decodeAudioData) into the same 0.1 s RMS/peak windows, compared within a measured tolerance.

where: tests/full-unchanged.html KEYS (FU3) and the suite guard fu980Wanted() in tests/tests.js
what: A new shortcut written with e.key passes both the probe and its suite guard. FU3 presses a fixed KEYS list, and the guard reads only `e.code === '…'`, ⌘-letter, arrow, digit and '?' patterns. keyf2: `else if (e.key === 'f' || e.key === 'F') { … FM.timeline.zoomBy(1.5); }` added to Full's window keydown handler. The same key written as `e.code === 'KeyF'` is seen by the guard and would turn the suite red. Shortcuts in any other keydown listener are unread too.

where: tests/full-unchanged.html FU5 (injects tests.js as a script into the app frame) and tools/_fu_gate.py INSTRUMENT_FILES / PROBE_FILES
what: tests/tests.js is served from the tree to both sides and runs inside the measured app frame at FU5. Its top-level statements run against the app before the sanitiser, save and load checks. It is still not instrument, so a Simple release may change it together with app code. The same change to tests/full-unchanged.html is refused, which shows the instrument rule is meant to cover this.
verified_by: rv926/gate_exp.py 'testsjs' on a scratch clone. App change, js/spine.js and a top-level line appended to tests/tests.js → only 'has not printed PASS'. The same release with tests/full-unchanged.html changed instead → 'it changes the instrument that judges it'. The injection is `var sc = D.createElement('script'); sc.textContent = src; D.body.appendChild(sc);` with D the app document.
fix: Do not execute tests.js in the probe. Take kitchen921 from HEAD's tests.js by extracting that function's source, or move the fixture builder into the probe (the instrument). Putting tests.js into INSTRUMENT_FILES would block every Simple release that adds tests.

where: tools/_fu_gate.py HOOKS ('the layer’s sm key', 'FM.storage.hydrating', 'a pick', 'a "Simple mode" marker') and REGION_HEAD (FM.editor\w*, FM.spine\w* prefixes)

Each of these lines, added in an ordinary 'queue 975' release, was refused: `const PAD = { sm: 4, md: 8, lg: 16 };`, `.chip.sm { … }`, `.hm-card.hydrating { … }`, `el.classList.add('pick');`, `const fn = FM.eyedropper.pick;` and a comment mentioning 'simple mode'. Also, an ordinary helper named `FM.editorHints = function () {…}` ships quietly, because the hooks are anchored. No current shipped line matches a hook (scan clean), so these are latent, but every one is a common idiom.
